prize_parts.citation: for the development of base editing, the programmable chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand cleavage
for the conception and demonstration of targeted protein degradation by heterobifunctional PROTAC molecules

statement.case_for: I keep my round-1 configuration. Base editing (B024) is a mechanistically transparent chemical step: a deaminase tethered to a catalytically impaired Cas protein converts a defined base without a double-strand break, and adenine editing required an enzyme evolved to act on DNA because none existed. It has been replicated widely, has reached patients, and has a decisive originator in Liu, whose laboratory built both editor families and the evolved architecture. PROTACs (B009) turn a binder into a remover through a measurable ternary complex, with a clean founding paper in 2001 and a decade of independent mechanistic validation. I would anchor that citation on the heterobifunctional concept and its demonstration, not on any clinical outcome. Both parts are scientifically mature on mechanism and replication, and the pair fits the three-person cap.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weak point. Liu alone omits Komor and Gaudelli, who wrote the two foundational papers, and the Kondo and Nishida Target-AID priority question is unresolved. Crews and Deshaies omit Sakamoto and Kim, who cannot be seated, and the cereblon and glue lineage of Handa and Ito, plus Ciulli and Gray. No PROTAC is an approved drug, and base editing can be read as a follow-on to the 2020 genome-editing prize. The two parts also share a theme (designed molecules acting on biological machinery) more than a method, so the pairing is coherent but not tight. If the committee judges Liu alone indefensible, the honest fallback is B024 as a single-achievement prize with Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, not a six-name pair.

responses.point: Chabes proposes B024 as the whole prize with Liu, Komor and Gaudelli, stressing that adenine base editing required evolving TadA to act on DNA, and noting that the 2020 prize and durability questions remain.
responses.response: I agree with your mechanistic argument: the evolved deaminase and the double-strand-break-free outcome are what make this chemistry, and that answers the follow-on objection for me. Where we differ is on how to carry Komor and Gaudelli. Their papers are foundational, but they were first authors in a programme that Liu conceived and directed, and the citation can name the two editor classes without seating the trainees. A single-part trio would also leave out a second mature achievement that the cap otherwise lets us honour. I would move to your trio only if the expert reports show the credit really divides three ways, or if the committee finds the PROTAC part premature.

responses.point: Somfai argues that base editing is largely protein engineering on top of the 2020 prize, and ranks PROTACs low because much of the mechanism is biology, while placing B003 first.
responses.response: I take the protein-engineering objection seriously, and it is why I want the citation to name the chemical conversion, deamination of a defined base, not genome editing in general. The 2020 prize recognised programmable cleavage; converting a base without cleavage is a different chemical outcome. On B003 I still respect the case and keep it as an alternative, but the 2010 cross-coupling prize and the Kosugi and Migita precursors make the third seat contestable in a way the two designed-molecule candidacies are not. Pairing B003 with Liu would also give a prize with no shared theme, which I think weakens it more than the B024 and B009 pairing does.

responses.point: Aqvist frames PROTACs as induced proximity and offered to shift the credit toward Handa if the molecular-glue lineage is judged the mature core of degradation.
responses.response: I understand the shift, but I would resist it. Handa's cereblon target identification is the basis of the glue branch and is important, but it is a distinct history from the heterobifunctional concept, and merging them in one citation would be wrong on priority. Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the bifunctional design in 2001, and the later cereblon and VHL ligands built on that concept. I would keep the citation narrow to the heterobifunctional concept, and if the committee prefers the glue lineage it should be a separate decision for another year, not a swap inside this configuration.

responses.point: Linke wants the PROTAC citation to rest on recruitment of the ubiquitin-proteasome system and asks whether Liu alone can be defended and what Target-AID priority does to the names.
responses.response: I accept your wording of recruitment of the ubiquitin-proteasome system as a mechanistic description and have kept it implicit in the citation through the heterobifunctional design. On Liu alone, my answer to your chair question is yes, provided the citation names the programmable chemical conversion without cleavage so that the trainees' papers are covered by the achievement description. On Target-AID, I regard it as an open priority point and will want the record checked; since it is a contemporaneous, different architecture, I expect it to change the wording or the alternatives more than the name list, but I would reconsider if the dates favour Kondo and Nishida.

uncertainties: Whether the expert reports support Liu alone, or a wider group, given Komor, Gaudelli, Kondo and Nishida.
Whether Target-AID has a priority claim that should change who is credited.
Whether the PROTAC part is premature without an approved drug, or whether the 2001 concept and mechanistic validation suffice.
Whether the committee reads base editing as a distinct chemical achievement rather than an extension of the 2020 prize.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the credited names. I am a Stockholm University colleague of Xiaodong Zou, whose leading candidacies (B025, B060) are not part of my configuration. My own research area, respiratory enzymes, is far from both preferred parts, and my opening first choice, nitrogenase (B038), is not part of my final position.
